activity-date.narrative: Planned start date of the activity

sector.narrative: 1.1 By 2030, eradicate extreme poverty for all people everywhere, currently measured as people living on less than $1.25 a day

8.3 Promote development-oriented policies that support productive activities, decent job creation, entrepreneurship, creativity and innovation, and encourage the formalization and growth of micro-, small- and medium-sized enterprises, including through access to financial services
8.5 By 2030, achieve full and productive employment and decent work for all women and men, including for young people and persons with disabilities, and equal pay for work of equal value
Output 3.1. Increased capacity of Member States to formulate and implement national employment policies in response to the COVID-19 crisis
Output 3.4. Increased capacity of Member States to promote peaceful, stable and resilient societies through decent work

tag.narrative: This activity is implemented partially in response to the COVID-19 pandemic

title.narrative: Output 3.4. Increased capacity of ILO constituents to promote peaceful, stable and resilient societies through decent work

description.narrative:
In 2020-2021, within the framework of the Joint Programme on Local Governance and Decentralized Service Delivery, UN-JPLG (Phase III), the regional governments of Puntland and Somaliland implemented sixty-two infrastructure projects with a total cost of over 4 million USD aimed at creating decent jobs and fostering social cohesion and peace building. Out of the 62 projects, 37 were implemented in Puntland, while the remaining 25 projects were implemented in Somaliland.
The implementing bodies, including the Ministry of Public Works and local governments from the two regions, built sustainable capacity to deliver equitable and sustainable services that promote economic development and peace building through decent work that can maximize job creation in rural communities.
Implementation capacity and the participation of local small-scale contractors in the delivery of public works have substantially increased through the provision of technical and managerial skills training in the use of local resource-based approaches relating to rural infrastructure development and maintenance.
The regional governments of Puntland and Somaliland have adapted and rolled out OSH measures and COVID-19 protocols on the prevention of the spread of the pandemic, which is enforced during implementation all public works projects. The ILO provided technical support to the Ministry of Public Works by developing planning, procurement and financial management procedures and documents. The ILO also developed training material on various thematic areas. From October 2020 to April 2021, the ILO trained central and local government officials as well as selected local contractors from the regions. The training pertained a range of areas required to implement and monitor labour-intensive works, including technical skills in the area of road infrastructure building construction works, required labour practices, and work planning and contract management, among others. Along the process, the ILO supported the Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs to adjust labour practices for labour-intensive works in response to the COVID-19 crisis.
